tells.1: The uniformly packaged stakeholder bullets and abstract phrases such as “Preserve match quality” suggest template-driven polish.
tells.2: “This causes four problems” introduces an unusually tidy stakeholder inventory; otherwise, little stands out.
tells.3: The repeated casual substitutions—“sit uncovered,” “actually accept,” “bunch up,” “in the loop”—feel like a deliberate conversational rewrite.
tells.5: “What this costs” feels like an editorial flourish added to otherwise conventional PRD prose, especially before “Agencies bear the cost.”

reason: Version 6 best balances natural language, scanability, and precision for a working PRD; version 4 feels like an unfinished human draft but ranks last on skilled execution. These are stylistic judgments, not authorship findings, and even version 6 needs to distinguish an escalated visit from a successfully rescheduled one.
